chandra: Heads-up — starting a FlashAttention v3 integration run. Goal: land flashv3 as an option in kernel chooser with safe fallbacks. Need kernel selection heuristics + feature-flagged rollout plan. TL;DR: canary -> perf verification -> staged percent rollout -> FF off if p95 regresses >5% or errors spike.
ben: +1. Can we list the concrete checks we want in the canary phase? seq len distribution, kv hit rates, batch size distribution, p50/p95 token latency, and error rate.
alice: Also add memory pressure metrics and OOM count. Flashv3 changes KV access patterns in the paged path and could surface mem cliffs.
eva: Proposed quick bench command: `./bench --kernel flashv3 --seq 128,512,1024 --batch-targets 8,32,128 --kv-paged` capture latency and throughput csv. We should compare to flashv2 baseline.
frank: I pushed a small harness in infra/bench that emits CSV with fields: kernel,seq,bs,throughput,tokens/sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,ooms,mem_p50_mb. Sample output: ```kernel,seq,bs,throughput,tokens/s,p50_ms,p95_ms,ooms,mem_p50_mb
flashv2,1024,32,1200,24000,18,56,0,13240
flashv3,1024,32,1320,26400,16,60,0,13120
``` Note: flashv3 p95 slightly higher at 60ms in this case — investigate tail behavior.
ben: That tail is suspicious. Could be batching heuristic interaction with KV paged fallback. For paged attention, larger seqs combine more pages and locking/serialization could cause tail spikes. Add trace sampling for tail requests.
chandra: Proposed canary plan: 1) create fflag `ff_flash_v3` default off; 2) enable for 1% of production traffic routed by route+seq heuristics for 48h; 3) collect metrics and compare to baseline windows; 4) expand to 10% then 50% if all gates pass. Gates: p95 delta <=+5%, error rate delta <=+0.1%, OOMs delta 0. Memory delta <=+8%. Rollback immediately if any gate trips.
alice: For routing heuristics, prefer: seq <=512 and kv_hit_rate >= 0.75 to start; avoid choosing flashv3 for long-seq cold-KV workloads. Can we auto-fallback per-request if latency exceeds a soft SLO?
eva: We can add per-request fallback: detect inflight kernel latency estimate > SLO and return request to legacy kernel. But need to ensure idempotence and not lose streaming state. That's tricky for streaming responses. Suggest limit fallbacks to non-streaming routes for now.
frank: Operational checklist: add SLI dashboard comparing `kernel=flashv3` vs `kernel=flashv2` for p50/p95/throughput/errors/ooms; add an alert rule for p95 delta > 5% sustained 10m; add an audit log entry when fflag toggled. Also ensure canary instances get double the sampling of profiling traces.
ben: Batching heuristics note: flashv3 shows better peak throughput at larger batch sizes but is sensitive to mixed seq distributions. Proposed algo: use weighted dynamic batching that caps effective batch size by 90th-percentile seq length to avoid head-of-line blocking. Config knobs: max_effective_batch, per-route_seq_threshold.
chandra: KV cache behavior: flashv3 path currently assumes monotonic KV eviction. Paged path introduces more frequent page lookups; recommend raising the per-instance KV prefetch window by 1.5x for canary to reduce page-induced stalls. Also instrument `kv_page_miss_ms` histogram.
alice: For the feature flag format: `ff_kernel_selector.flash_v3 = {enabled: false, criteria: {seq_max:512,kv_hit_min:0.75}}` We'll store criteria as JSON in feature flag store. Also add `force_kv_prefetch=true` toggle for canary hosts.
eva: Quick implementation note: in runtime router, add a lightweight decision function: if ff enabled and criteria matched -> try flashv3, else use fallback kernel. Keep decision idempotent and log kernel_choice metadata on request.
frank: Can we run a small prod-sim scale test on staging with traffic generator matching prod seq distribution? If staging results look good, proceed to 1% canary.
chandra: Yes — @frank can you carve out a 2h slot tonight to run sim? Add deploy-bot check to schedule. :calendar:
deploy-bot: Schedule request received. Candidate slot 2025-11-17T03:00Z reserved on infra-staging for 2h. Runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/flashv3-canary 
ben: After canary, we should run a focused stress test for KV page storms: synthetic workload that alternates keys to drive low kv_hit rates and measure tail. If tail > threshold, we should add a per-request circuit breaker to block flashv3 for that route.
chandra: Decision owners: kernel-chooser (ben), kv/paged (alice), bench infra (frank), rollout ops (eva). Next steps: ben to create PR for ff + routing, frank to run staging sim, alice to add kv telemetry, eva to wire alerts. Meet tomorrow 11:00 to review staging results.
eva: Acked. I'll create the alert dashboards and add the SLO compare queries.
alice: I'll add `kv_page_miss_ms` and `kv_prefetch_hit_rate` to tracer and push a small patch.
ben: I'll draft the PR and a short canary playbook doc with explicit rollback commands and metrics to collect.
frank: I'll kick off the sim tonight and post results here. Expect a short CSV and perf profile.
chandra: Thanks all — try to keep messages in this thread for the record. If anyone hits a blocker ping me directly. :rocket:
